If I rank x first, I might not get in due to the high demand. If I rank z first, I might get in, but I prefer x. Ranking y first seems counterproductive since I like x and z more. Ranking w first is definitely not optimal.

Then, I rank z second as my next best option and a school I'm also a high priority applicant for. I rank y third, as it's better than w, but less preferred than x and z. Finally, I rank w last. This strategy maximizes my chance of getting into my most preferred school, x, while still providing good fallback options.
